history: Version 1: 57 cases. Rust refused known ignorable rows and image/offload as the native limits ignorable and event-type.

Version 2: Rust restores image/offload with the catalog projection and known ignorable rows. The ignorable and event-type limits are removed and projection added. known-ignorable-hook-result and known-ignorable-user-message lose their rust overrides, and known-ignorable-tool-update and image-offload name restore causes; their version-1 TypeScript outcomes are unchanged. The 42 cases after unknown-type-before-fallback-header were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.
Round 2 of version 2 added 19 cases for the independent review's obligations, written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran on them.

Version 3: Rust restores every number spelled as JSON.stringify writes its value. usage-fraction and context-fraction lose their rust overrides; their version-2 TypeScript outcomes are unchanged. negative-zero-in-user-message still witnesses the number limit, which remains for spellings no writer produces.

Version 4: Rust restores payloads of any depth, which it parses, copies, compares, and drops without recursing, and the depth limit is removed. user-message-depth loses its rust override; its version-3 TypeScript outcome is unchanged.

Version 5: 122 cases. Rust carries a request header's config members outside LlmCallConfig through restoration as TypeScript does, and the config-member limit is removed. config-member loses its rust override; its version-4 TypeScript outcome is unchanged. config-object-member, config-index-member, config-proto-member, and config-duplicate-member were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran, and both harnesses now also compare the restored request header as JSON.stringify text, so member order, array-index keys first, is checked.
